### About This Round

Koppla, a Germany-based company offering an intuitive and collaborative scheduling platform for construction sites, has raised €6 million in its latest funding round. The round was led by [Newion](https://seedtable.com/companies/newion-investments), with additional investments from [Brandenburg Kapital](https://seedtable.com/investors/brandenburg-kapital) and angel investors Martin Rodeck, Thorsten Krauß, Ingo Holz, and Andreas Beckmann. The investors bring valuable sector knowledge in construction and real estate, which is expected to aid Koppla’s growth in the industry.[1](https://www.koppla.de/blog/koppla-sammelt-6-millionen-euro-ein)

Koppla’s scheduling platform is designed to streamline and optimize construction project management by connecting field crews with office staff. The platform adapts in real time to changes on construction sites, allowing tasks to be updated, idle time to be cleared, and work to continue even if there are disruptions such as subcontractors dropping out or changes in the project scope. This system enables more efficient decision-making, reducing costly delays and errors associated with outdated scheduling tools.[1](https://www.koppla.de/blog/koppla-sammelt-6-millionen-euro-ein)

Leopold Lindner of Newion, commenting on the investment, emphasized the importance of Koppla’s solution in addressing significant challenges within the construction industry. He stated that the construction sector is under significant pressure to modernize and that Koppla offers a solution tailored to the specific needs of the industry, making it a compelling investment. The platform’s intuitive, collaborative approach aims to reduce silo thinking and improve the accuracy and timeliness of scheduling, making it a valuable tool for construction companies.[1](https://www.koppla.de/blog/koppla-sammelt-6-millionen-euro-ein)

Angel investor Martin Rodeck also highlighted the inefficiencies of traditional scheduling tools, which are often not usable in real-time and can lead to outdated project management decisions. According to Rodeck, Koppla’s platform eliminates these issues by offering an easy-to-use schedule that adapts in real time and connects all participating companies. He expressed his excitement about supporting Koppla in its mission to transform the construction industry.[1](https://www.koppla.de/blog/koppla-sammelt-6-millionen-euro-ein)

The €6 million raised in this funding round will be used to further develop Koppla’s platform and expand its customer base. Currently, the platform is used by more than 100 customers across 600 projects, managing a total project volume of over €3 billion. The company plans to use the funds to enhance its construction scheduling and control platform, focusing on improving its functionality and extending its reach within the construction sector. Additionally, Koppla intends to hire staff in key areas such as customer success, sales, product development, and technology to support its growth.[1](https://www.koppla.de/blog/koppla-sammelt-6-millionen-euro-ein)

The company’s founders, Marco Trippler and Lasse Steffen, expressed their enthusiasm for the future of Koppla. Trippler noted that the funding brings the company closer to its vision of developing a simple, holistic scheduling solution for the construction industry. Steffen added that there is strong demand for solutions that simplify project management and replace legacy tools, and the new funding will help accelerate the development of Koppla’s platform to meet this demand.[1](https://www.koppla.de/blog/koppla-sammelt-6-millionen-euro-ein)

Koppla was founded in 2020 by three school friends, including Marco Trippler and Lasse Steffen, after they recognized the lack of data-driven tools in the construction industry. Since then, the company has grown to a team of over 20 employees. The platform is already being used by several top construction firms in the DACH region, and the company has established a strong presence in the market, helping construction companies manage their projects more efficiently.[1](https://www.koppla.de/blog/koppla-sammelt-6-millionen-euro-ein)

With this new funding, Koppla is poised to further expand its platform, improve its product offering, and grow its customer base, positioning itself as a key player in the modernization of the construction industry.[1](https://www.koppla.de/blog/koppla-sammelt-6-millionen-euro-ein)
